extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited to act as peer reviewers or panellists for BBSRC/UKRI grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for carrying out peer review of BBSRC (UKRI) standard grant proposals, including procedural steps, expected content and tone of reviews, policy compliance, and special considerations (e.g., COVID-19, AI). Intended for expert reviewers and panel members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline of the standard process for assessing standard grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are considered by two or more peer reviewers; applicants provide a principal investigator response to peer reviewer comments; proposals, reviews, and PI responses are considered by the assessment panel; the panel provides a rank ordered list of proposals in order of funding priority; the panels' recommendations are considered internally by BBSRC and a final decision is taken on the list of awards to be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide BBSRC, when requested, with a review by the due date specified and in accordance with the reviewer guidance in the UKRI Funding Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to meet a review request, notify BBSRC by declining via the Funding Service within five working days of the request so an alternative reviewer can be sought without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow reviewer form and Funding Service guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the reviewer form using the specific guidance provided in the UKRI Funding Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidance is available on the reviewer form that you are asked to complete; read guidance on how reviewers use the UKRI Funding Service before completing your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to UKRI policies and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold UKRI’s policies, standards and guidance in support of good research practices when conducting peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with UKRI policies (for example counter fraud and bribery policy) and the UKRI principles of assessment and decision-making which explain core principles and expectations for assessment processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics (DORA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles or to assess an individual scientist’s contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in line with BBSRC/UKRI's commitment to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional external material — anonymity risk
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposal includes a link to a website with additional information, reviewers are not required to consider it when providing comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do choose to look at linked material, be aware it may compromise your anonymity to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on generative AI in assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and panellists are not permitted to use generative AI tools to develop their assessment, including to correct language, spelling, grammar and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using these tools can potentially compromise the confidentiality of applicants' ideas. See UKRI's policy on the use of generative AI for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced, objective tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be balanced and objective; avoid confrontational or emotive tone or language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels can only assess applications if peer reviews are balanced and objective. Remember applicants will see peer review as part of the right to reply; subjective or unbalanced language makes it difficult for applicants to respond effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve reviewer anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not identify yourself within your comments (inadvertently or overtly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants do not see reviewer identities; preserving anonymity helps reviewers express views freely. Panels are made aware of reviewer identities, but applicants are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient detail and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overly brief comments; provide justified, detailed comments so panels can make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BBSRC panels need a clear idea of strengths and weaknesses as identified by reviewers. Comments should be justified so the moderating panel can make an informed decision based on expert peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address expected areas of assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should critically examine the proposal across expected areas rather than giving only high-level comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure research questions, context and methodologies are considered when writing peer reviews for BBSRC. Identify both strengths and weaknesses for effective moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must follow UKRI's policy on declarations of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the UKRI policy on declarations of interest and declare any conflicts as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of COVID-19 impacts on track record
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing the research project, consider unequal impacts of COVID-19-related disruption on applicants' track records and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the capability of the applicant and team to deliver the proposed research. Applicants were advised to base applications on information available at submission and to highlight known impacts; you should assess the project as written and note any changes that might be required later. Potential complications related to COVID-19 should not affect your assessment or the score you give the project. Refer also to UKRI principles of assessment and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons a review may be considered unusable
rubrics_metrics.description: Common reasons why BBSRC might consider a review unusable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: confrontational or emotive tone or language; reviewer identifies themselves within comments; comments are too brief; reviewer has not addressed the areas expected for effective peer review and there is little or no critical examination of the proposal. BBSRC will not use reviews that do not meet its criteria for appropriateness and value to applicants and panels.
